title: Evaluating Deep Learning Brain Tumour Classification Performance on African Neuroimaging Data with Grad-CAM Explainability and Offline Mobile Deployment
design: Domain-shift evaluation of a transfer-learning CNN; specificity / false-positive-rate framing; annotation-free Grad-CAM metrics
sample: 7,023 training MRIs (Kaggle) + Nigerian 0.3T / 1.5T clinical MRI set
summary: Measures how much a Western-trained brain tumour classifier degrades on low-field African MRI, and whether its Grad-CAM explanations stay trustworthy. Self-funded, 16-week execution window (27 Aug – 22 Dec 2026).

title: Doctors' Perspectives of Hospital Preparedness for Mass Casualty Incidents in Conflict-Affected Regions of Sudan: A Multicenter Qualitative Study
role: Co-author (5th of 12), SCSD Lab of Trauma Surgery
design: Multicentre qualitative study; semi-structured interviews; thematic analysis
sample: 31 trauma surgeons across 5 tertiary hospitals, Jan–Feb 2025
summary: Only 4.2% of respondents reported adequate equipment; 20.8% reported no preparedness and 8.3% felt fully prepared. START triage was applied inconsistently under overcrowding and staffing gaps.

title: Trauma Surgeons' Preparedness for Mass Casualty Incidents During the Armed Conflict in Sudan (2025): A Multicenter Qualitative Study
role: Co-author (5th of 12), SCSD Lab of Trauma Surgery
design: Multicentre qualitative study; in-depth interviews; thematic content analysis
sample: 24 trauma surgeons across 5 tertiary hospitals, Jan–Feb 2025
summary: 70.8% reported inadequate critical equipment, yet 79.2% felt confident managing MCIs, with no link between confidence and prior training. None had received psychological support; busy hospitals saw up to 3,500 MCI cases a month.

title: Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices on Stroke Manifestations and Complications Among Sudanese Population, Khartoum 2025
status: Graded A; journal manuscript in preparation
design: Descriptive cross-sectional survey; structured pretested questionnaire
summary: 431 of 473 had heard of stroke, but only a minority could identify key symptoms or risk factors. Education was the strongest predictor of KAP scores; knowledge and attitudes correlated strongly, knowledge and practice only weakly.

title: Um Katti Hospital Post-Conflict Epidemiological Baseline Assessment, Karari Locality, Khartoum State
status: Submitted to Dept. of Community Medicine
design: Household survey, key informant interviews, structured observation checklists
sample: 262 households (1,355 persons); 26 key informant interviews; catchment of ~66,000
summary: Malaria made up 49.7% of 13,418 OPD visits; 22.9% of assessed under-fives had severe acute malnutrition; doctor-to-population ratio was 1:8,250. Rural residency field work with a real research component.
